texts.preamble: State vs Naresh Gupta on 9 October, 2025 In The Court Of Preeti: Judicial Magistrate First Class - 03 (Central) Tis Hazari Courts: Delhi State Vs. : Naresh Gupta Fir No : 128/2011 U/s : 279/337/338 Ipc P.S. : Ip Estate Judgment:
texts.facts: The genesis of the prosecution story is that on 18.10.2011, at about 3:15 PM at Ring Road, near WHO building, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS IP Estate, accused was found driving car bearing no. DL-3CBF-7409 in rash manner and endangering the life and safety of others and caused grievous injuries to Vijay Singh Malik and Suman Kumar and caused simple injuries to Sheetal and Anil Gupta. Thereafter, the alleged offending vehicle was taken into possession by the police after which its mechanical inspection was conducted. It is stated in the chargesheet that the alleged offending vehicle was being driven by accused at the relevant time. After completion of investigation, the chargesheet for offences u/s 279/337/338 IPC was submitted for trial of accused. 2. Thereafter, the cognizance of the offences was taken by the Ld. Predecessor Court and on the basis of material available on record, notice of accusation for offences u/s 279/337/338 IPC was State vs Naresh Gupta on 9 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98269053/ 1 framed and served upon accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 3. The accused admitted registration of FIR No. 128/2011 Ex.A1, preparation of certificate u/s 65-B Indian Evidence Act Ex. A-2, medical papers of injured Shyamveer prepared by Doctor Ajeet Kumar Ex. A-3 and the concerned witnesses were accordingly dropped from list of witnesses. 4. In order to establish guilt of the accused, prosecution has examined 13 witnesses in all. 4.1 PW-1 Vijay Singh Malik deposed that on 18/10/2011, he was posted as food Supply Officer at Enforcement Food Supply Department, K, Block Govt. of Delhi. He received information that a truck bearing no. DL-1LM-4622 (Tata 709) was carrying PDS wheat and same had been stopped in front of WHO Building. Thereafter, he alongwith Sh. Suman Kumar, SI Anti Hoarding Cell and Inspector Shyamvir reached at the spot. On the spot, the informer met them and tempo TATA 709 bearing no. DL-1LM-4622 was also present. He further stated that the bags of wheat were loaded in said truck and they started checking the wheat bags. He was standing behind the said truck and SI Suman Kumar and Inspector Shyamveer were planning to climb the above said truck. In the meantime, one car bearing no. DL-3CBF-7407(make I-10) was coming from the side of Sarai Kalan Khan and was going to ISBT Kashmere Gate. The driver of the said car was driving the car in high speed and rash and negligent manner and hit the above said tempo and due to which he alongwith SI Suman Kumar and Inspector Shyamveer were got serious injuries. The informer Anil Gupta and driver of the above said tempo were also got hurt. The PCR van reached on the spot and they were taken to LNJP hospital. The driver of the car was apprehended by the police on the spot. At about 5:00 PM, he was shifted to Ganga Ram Hospital due to serious injury. IO recorded his statement. This witness was cross-examined by Ld. counsel for defence. 4.2 PW-2 Sh. Shyambir Singh deposed that incident was of 18/10/2011. On that day, he was posted as Inspector at Food & Supply, Enforcement Branch, ITO, Delhi. On date of incident, he alongwith his senior officer Sh. Vijay Singh Malik (FSO, Enforcement F & S) and SI Suman Kumar (Incharge Anti Hoarding Cell F &S) reached at Ring Road, near WHO Building, Delhi at about 03.00 PM. On the said road, one tempo no. Dl-1-LM-4622 Tata-709 was found standing and the same was loaded with the sacks of wheat. One public person namely Anil Gupta was found present there and he told them that the said tempo was loaded with the sacks of wheat of PDS. SI Suman Kumar and Sh. Vijay Singh Malik started climbing on the said tempo for inspection of the sacks of wheat present in the said tempo and he was standing behind the said tempo and was inquiring with the owner of the said tempo namely Sheetal. At the same time at about 03.15 PM, one car i-10 no. DL-3-C-BF-7409 came from the side of Sarai Kale Khan and its driver was driving the said car in rash and negligent manner and hit against them. Due to the said incident, SI Suman Kumar, SI Vijay Singh Malik, Anil Gupta, driver of said tempo namely Sheetal and he sustained injuries. PCR Van came to the spot and they took them to LNJP Hospital where doctor examined all of them. Doctor told him that their muscles had been ruptured and advised him to do the "Sikai with Ice". He was having pain in his leg. He left the hospital and was going to his house and in the way, he had severe pain in his leg. So he went to Jivan Jyoti Clinic & Hospital, GTB Chowk, Dilshad Garden in emergency ward where doctors State vs Naresh Gupta on 9 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98269053/ 2 examined him and did X-ray of his leg and doctor told him that he had sustained fracture in his right leg. The person who was driving the i-10 car was accused. The said incident took place due to rash and negligent driving of accused. 4.3 PW-3 Sh. Manohar Lal deposed that on 19.10.2011, he mechanically inspected vehicle/car bearing number DL3C AF 7409 and Mini Truck Number DLIL M 4644 at PS I P Estate at the request of IO. He prepared the detailed mechanical inspection reports. He found fresh damages on the body of vehicles as mentioned in the detailed reports. Vehicles were found fit for road test. This witness was not cross-examined by Ld. counsel for defence. 4.4 PW-4 Anil Gupta deposed that on 18.10.2011 at about 2.30 pm, he was going towards ITO and at about 2.30 pm, he was at Ring Road, Bhairo Road. He saw a tempo number DL-1LM-4622 loaded with wheat. He informed Sh. V.S. Malik, Food and Supply Officer and Sh. V S Malik asked to get the tempo stopped and after sometime, V.S. Malik came along with his team member. The Food and Supply Officers were trying to board the said tempo. In the meantime, one I-10 car DL-3CBF-7409 came in a rash and negligent manner and hit tempo and him. The Food and Supply Officers and he sustained injuries. The accused was driving the said i-10 car in a rash and negligent manner. 4.5 PW-5 Retd. SI Sukhbir Singh deposed that on 18.10.2011, he was posted in PCR, Central Zone, Delhi as Head constable. He was on duty at PCR van Oscar 22 and their base was IP Metro station. On that day, at about 3.00 pm, information was received from Oskar 1 regarding the road accident near WHO building. He along with staff reached there and found the tempo no. DL-1LM-4622 and car no.DL-3CBL-7409 lying in accidental condition. Two persons were lying there in injured condition whose names were revealed as Sheetal and Shyamvir. They took both the injured persons to LNJP Hospital. 4.6 PW-6 ASI Satpal deposed that on 18.10.2011, he was posted in PCR, Central Zone, Delhi as Head constable. On that day, he was on duty at PCR van Oscar 21 and their base was near WHO building. They heard noise of hitting of two vehicles. They reached at that spot and found the tempo no. DL-1LM-4622 and car no. DL-3CBL-7409 lying in accidental condition. Two persons were lying there in injured condition whose names were revealed as Vijay and Suman. 4.7 PW-7 Inspector Nafe Singh deposed that on 24.10.2011, he was posted at MACT Cell, Central Delhi as SI. The case file was received to him for further investigation. During investigation, he recorded the statement of PWs. He deposited the MLC of injured persons in the hospital for obtaining nature of injuries. The nature of injury was opined as grievous and simple respectively and thereafter, he collected the documents of vehicles involved in the accident and got verified the same. After completion of the investigation, chargesheet was filed. 4.8 PW-8 ASI Md. Ibrahim deposed that on 18.10.2011, he was posted as Constable at PS E.P. Estate. On that day, he joined the investigation in this case. He alongwith the IO reached at the spot State vs Naresh Gupta on 9 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98269053/ 3 in front of WHO building where the car and TATA 709 were lying in accidental condition. The driver of car was also there. IO left the driver of car in his supervision and he proceeded to hospital. After some time, he came back at the spot with the injured and prepared the rukka and handed over the same for registration of the FIR. He went to the PS and got registered the case. After some time, he again reached at the spot and he handed over the copy of the FIR, rukka and certificate under Section 65-B of Indian Evidence Act to the IO. IO inspected the site and prepared the site plan. IO arrested the accused. The abovesaid car and TATA 709 were taken into possession. IO seized the document of the car. IO seized the document of TATA 709. IO seized the DL of the accused. 4.9 PW-9 SI Joginder Singh deposed that on 18.10.2011, he was posted at P.S. I.P.Estate as HC. On that day, he received DD no. 18 A regarding the accident at Ring Road WHO Building ITO, Delhi. He alongwith Ct. Ibrahim reached at spot, where Tempo no. DL 1LM 4622 and car no. DL 3CBF 7409 were found in accidental condition. He was taken into custody and handed over to Ct. Ibrahim. The PCR already had taken the injured person to hospital. He left Ct. Ibrahim at spot with accused for supervision of spot and he went to hospital where he collected the MLC of injured persons Vijay Kumar Malik, Suman, Sheetal Sada and others. He recorded the statement of injured Sheetal Sada. Thereafter, he returned at spot alongwith complainant. He prepared rukka and got registered the case through Ct. Ibrahim who went to P.S. and got registered the FIR. He inspected the site at the instance of the complainant and prepared site plan. Ct. Ibrahim again came at the spot, who gave him copy of FIR and rukka. The accused was arrested at the identification of complainant. He seized offending car and truck TATA 407. He seized the document of car and said truck. He also seized the D/L of accused. Both the vehicles were taken to PS. Both the vehicles were mechanically inspected and he collected the mechanical inspection reports. He recorded the statement of witnesses. The MLC of injured person were deposited for obtaining the nature of injury. The nature of injury on the MLC of injured Suman was opined grievous, therefore, he added section 338 IPC. Thereafter the investigation was transferred to MACT Cell, Central, Delhi and he returned the case file to MHC(R). 4.10 PW-10 Inspector Suman Kumar deposed that it was 18.10.2011. He was posted as SI at the office of Food and Supply Dept. GNCT Delhi. On that day, he was directed by the FSO enforcement Sh. Vijay Singh Malik to accompany him regarding checking of Illegal Food Grains carrying in vehicles. At about 03.00 PM, he, Sh. V.S. Malik and Inspector Shyam Veer were present at Ring Road in front of WHO Building where a TATA 407 bearing no. DL-1LM-4622 was stationed loaded with Gunny Bags of food grains. One person namely Anil was also there. At the instruction of Sh. V S Malik, he started to check the gunny bags loaded with food grains. He and V S Malik were just behind the vehicle TATA 407 bearing no. DL-1LM-4622. One I-10 car bearing no. DL-3CBF-7409 came and hit them and TATA 407 resulting of which they sustained injuries. Accused Naresh Kumar Gupta was driving the said offending car. He sustained injuries/multiple fracture on his right leg. PCR came and took them (Injured persons) to LNJP Hospital where they received medical treatment. From LNJP Hospital, he was shifted to Saint Stephen Hospital Kashmeri Gate Delhi. During investigation, on 20.12.2011, he was present at MACT Cell Rajinder Nagar Delhi where he saw the accused Naresh Gupta with IO of the case SI Nafe Singh and he identified him as the driver of aforesaid offending car at the time of accident, who was driving the said car bearing no. State vs Naresh Gupta on 9 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98269053/ 4 DL3CBF7409 in rash and negligent manner. This witness was cross- examined by Ld. counsel for defence. 4.11 PW-11 Dr. Vivek Kumar deposed that on 09.12.2011, he was posted at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital in Plastic and Cosmetic Surgery(Unit-2) as a Consultant. On that day, he advised the patient namely Vijay Singh Malik for follow up vide letter no. MRD/1/2011 dated 09.12.2011. 4.12 PW-12 Dr. Arvind deposed that on 18.10.2011, he was posted at LNJP Hospital as CMO in accident and emergency department. The MLCs no. 166758/11, 166754/11, 166753/11, 166782/11 and 166921/11 were prepared by the concerned doctors under his supervision. 4.13 PW-13 Dr. Yogesh deposed that he was a summoned witness to depose on behalf of Dr. Shailender. The nature of injury is grievous on the basis of X-Ray report no. 5842-45. The MLC already Ex. P-4 upon which mentioned at point A the nature of injury is simple from orthopedic point of view on the basis of X-ray report. 5. Thereafter, PE was closed and matter was fixed for recording of statement of accused. 6. After prosecution evidence, the statement of accused u/s 281 Cr.PC r/w 313 Cr.P.C was recorded wherein all the incriminating circumstances were put to him to which he stated that he is innocent and he had been falsely implicated in the case. Accused opted not to lead DE. 7. Thereafter, matter was fixed for final arguments.
texts.arguments: 8. Ld. counsel for the accused argued that accused was not driving the vehicle negligently and the accident was caused due to negligence of complainant and injured persons. He further argued that site plan was not prepared at the instance of complainant and no public witness has been cited as witness. He further argued that there are contradictions in the testimony of PW-1 and PW-4. With these submissions, he prayed that benefit of doubt be given to the accused. Per contra, Ld. APP for the State argued that there is sufficient material available on record to render conviction to the accused as the guilt of the accused has been proved beyond reasonable doubt. Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled as Shyam Babu Vs. State of UP, AIR 2012 SC 3311, held that the testimony of injured witness stands on higher pedestal.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 8. Ld. counsel for the accused argued that accused was not driving the vehicle negligently and the accident was caused due to negligence of complainant and injured persons. He further argued that site plan was not prepared at the instance of complainant and no public witness has been cited as witness. He further argued that there are contradictions in the testimony of PW-1 and PW-4. With these submissions, he prayed that benefit of doubt be given to the accused.
texts.respondent_arguments: Per contra, Ld. APP for the State argued that there is sufficient material available on record to render conviction to the accused as the guilt of the accused has been proved beyond reasonable doubt.
texts.other_lawyer_arguments: Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled as Shyam Babu Vs. State of UP, AIR 2012 SC 3311, held that the testimony of injured witness stands on higher pedestal.
